title: VeriVoice

listing.shortDescription: An intelligent multi-agent voice platform designed to automate business conversations and workflows.
listing.fullDescription: VeriVoice is an intelligent voice automation platform that enables businesses to deploy specialised AI agents for customer conversations, qualification and task execution. Rather than one general-purpose bot, each agent owns a narrow remit — reception, qualification, booking, follow-up — and hands off to the next with full context. Every call is transcribed, scored and written back to the customer's CRM, and any caller can reach a human by asking.

cover.imageAlt: Abstract diagram of a multi-agent voice routing system with connected conversation nodes

closing.clientOverview: A business losing about a third of its inbound calls to voicemail outside staffed hours — and most of those never returned. Earlier voice automation had failed badly: latency was long enough that callers spoke over the agent and conversations collapsed, and call outcomes were logged by hand so the pipeline data could not be trusted.
closing.conclusion: VeriVoice now carries the calls that previously went to voicemail through natural, low-latency conversations with barge-in interruption, handing over to a person instantly when asked — context included. Multi-agent design with narrow tool permissions keeps the automation contained and safe, structured outcomes land in the CRM on every call, and an evaluation suite means model changes ship only when they measure up.

features.title: Specialised agent roster
features.description: Reception, qualification, booking and follow-up agents each with their own instructions, tools and success criteria.

features.title: Context-preserving handoff
features.description: Agents transfer the caller along with the full conversation state, so nobody is asked the same question twice.

features.title: Sub-second turn-taking
features.description: Streaming speech recognition and synthesis tuned so the agent responds at conversational speed and yields when interrupted.

features.title: Live calendar booking
features.description: Availability is read and slots are held in real time during the call, with confirmation sent before hanging up.

features.title: Human escalation
features.description: Warm transfer to an available person on request, on low confidence, or on any topic flagged as out of scope.

features.title: Call analytics
features.description: Transcripts, outcome tagging, sentiment and per-agent quality scoring in one reviewable dashboard.

challenge.summary: The client was losing qualified enquiries outside office hours and burning senior time on calls that never needed a specialist. Earlier voice bots had been abandoned because callers found them slow and evasive.

points.title: Calls outside hours went nowhere
points.description: Roughly a third of inbound calls arrived outside staffed hours and went to voicemail, where most were never returned.

points.title: Latency broke the call
points.description: Previous systems had latency long enough that callers spoke over the agent and the conversation collapsed.

points.title: Untrusted call outcomes
points.description: Call outcomes were logged manually and inconsistently, so pipeline data could not be trusted.

points.title: Instant human handover
points.description: Any automated system had to hand over to a person instantly on request, without the caller repeating themselves.

solution.summary: We built a multi-agent architecture where each agent has one job, a small set of tools and an explicit escalation path — then optimised the audio pipeline until conversations felt natural.

points.title: Typed agent handoffs
points.description: Split the conversation into discrete agent roles with typed handoff contracts carrying full context.

points.title: End-to-end streaming
points.description: Streamed speech recognition and synthesis end to end, with barge-in detection so callers can interrupt naturally.

points.title: Narrow tool permissions
points.description: Gave each agent narrow, permissioned tool access — calendar, CRM, knowledge base — rather than open-ended system control.

points.title: Regression-tested changes
points.description: Built an evaluation suite of recorded scenarios so prompt and model changes are measured against regressions before release.

points.title: Structured CRM writes
points.description: Wrote structured outcomes back to the CRM on every call, removing manual logging entirely.

results.label: Call coverage
results.detail: Every inbound call answered, including nights and weekends.

results.label: Median response latency
results.detail: Measured from end of caller speech to first audio out.

results.label: Calls resolved without a human
results.detail: Across booking, qualification and routine enquiries.

results.label: Calls logged automatically
results.detail: Structured outcomes written to the CRM with no manual entry.

workflow.title: Call received
workflow.description: Twilio routes the call into the platform and opens a bidirectional audio stream.

workflow.title: Reception agent
workflow.description: Identifies the caller, establishes intent and selects the specialist agent to hand to.

workflow.title: Specialist agent
workflow.description: Runs its objective — qualification, booking or support — using its permitted tools.

workflow.title: System actions
workflow.description: Calendar slots are held, CRM records created and confirmations dispatched mid-call.

workflow.title: Outcome & handoff
workflow.description: Transcript, outcome and recording are written back, or the caller is warm-transferred to a person.

objectives: Answer calls outside staffed hours with no voicemail graveyard
Keep latency low enough for natural conversation
Hand over to a person instantly without repetition
Log every call outcome as structured CRM data
Ship model changes only against measured regressions
